Zinc
Likely effective for diarrhea and 
Wilson’s disease. Possibly effec-
tive for acne, age related macu-
lar degeneration, anemia, an-
orexia nervosa, attention deficit 
hyperactivity disorder, burns, 
common cold, dandruff, depres-
sion, diabetic foot ulcers, diaper 
rash, halitosis, gingivitis, herpes 
simplex virus, muscle cramps, 
radiation mucositis, osteoporo-
sis, peptic ulcers, pressure  
ulcers, sickle cell disease,  
vitamin A deficiency, warts
Doses vary depending on 
condition. 15-45 mg/day 
range is common. Much 
higher doses sometimes 
given for wound healing 
short term. Coordination 
of care recommended.
Mostly nontoxic below the UL of 
40 mg/day in adults. High Zn  
intake can deplete copper and 
can cause nausea, dermatitis, 
and copper deficient anemia.
Take Zn supplements  
with copper to prevent  
depletion of copper.
